## Ranked proposals

1. **A small “Changing Shoreline” table display using pattern FW-7.** The later workshop record describes paper cutouts casting bands of light and explains the changing-shoreline idea; the pattern record describes a portable three-band silhouette ([workshop notes](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt>), [pattern description](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt>)). Mara and her collaborator permit FW-7 in a free community educational display, with both makers credited ([FW-7 terms](<archive/03-rights/folded-water.txt>)). The shelf inventory lists card, blue scraps, scissors, and tape, though it was checked on October 2 and should be checked again ([craft-box note](<archive/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt>)). A previous prototype used similar materials ([materials note](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt>)).

   **Next step:** Confirm the materials are still available, make one paper prototype, and ask library staff to confirm a date for the table. Credit both makers on the display. The motorized lightbox from the old plan was never ordered and is unavailable ([old plan](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/old-plan.txt>); [resource note](<archive/04-resources/other-materials.txt>)). One archive note describes a two-slit version while the later workshop and pattern records describe three; no final-authoritative signoff is supplied, so confirm the intended pattern with the makers before producing multiples ([old copy](<archive/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt>)).

2. **A text-led “Tide Lines” educational display, without photographs or audio.** The concept concerns how changing water levels reshape familiar paths ([concept](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/concept.txt>)). Mara permits reuse of her captions and observation notes in free public educational displays ([Tide Lines rights](<archive/03-rights/tide-notes.txt>)). Those materials include two short captions and three dated water-level observations ([text fragments](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt>); [observations](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt>)). Up to twelve black-and-white pages are quoted at $8, within the $30 cap, though studio printing depends on printer availability ([printing quote](<archive/04-resources/printing-quote.txt>); [studio printing note](<archive/02-assets/notes/printing.txt>)).

   **Next step:** Draft a one-page display using only Mara’s permitted text, label the observations as informal field notes, and verify the historical claim about the path moving inland in 1981 against its original reference before including it ([research note](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt>)). Confirm printer availability and the library date before committing to production ([venue](<archive/04-resources/venue.txt>); [calendar](<archive/04-resources/calendar.txt>)).

## Unresolved possibility

**Tide Lines with photographs** remains a hypothesis, not a current proposal: the indexed images depict identifiable people, and their photographer’s agreement bars public display or exhibition without separate written consent. No later consent appears in the record ([photo terms](<archive/03-rights/photo-terms.txt>); [photo description](<archive/02-assets/notes/photo-description.txt>)). The files are also absent from this archive ([photo index](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/photos-index.txt>)). Do not use them unless the required consent is obtained and the actual files are available. Sound S-3 is similarly unavailable here, with ownership and public-use permission unconfirmed ([sound terms](<archive/03-rights/sound-terms.txt>); [sound index](<archive/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt>)).

## Scope and uncertainties

I reviewed the files returned by a recursive workspace inventory, including project notes, resource records, rights records, and archive notes; this does not establish that the textual archive contains every relevant record or asset. The venue is only tentatively available, and its date is not booked. Both proposals fit the stated free educational-display purpose and appear feasible within the stated weekend and budget, subject to the checks above ([request](<archive/04-resources/request.txt>); [venue](<archive/04-resources/venue.txt>)).## Ranked proposals

1. **A small Folded Water demonstration table**

   Recreate the FW-7 paper silhouette as a simple educational display: cut three horizontal slits in folded card, unfold it, and use movable blue paper bands to show how a repeated shape can suggest a changing shoreline. The workshop notes say movable bands make changes easy to notice, and the materials record says the prototype used white card, blue offcuts, and scissors ([demo notes](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt>), [materials](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt>)). The pattern description specifies three slits, though it is a verbal description and there is no finished stencil ([shape diagram](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt>)). The old-copy note describes two slits and does not supply authoritative signoff, so use the later three-slit description as the best available guide while treating the design as something to confirm with the makers ([old copy](<archive/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt>)).

   **Rights and limits:** Mara and the collaborator authorize the described pattern for a free community educational display, with credit to both makers; commercial resale is excluded ([Folded Water rights](<archive/03-rights/folded-water.txt>)). This supports the narrow proposed use. Do not add the indexed photos or the S-3 recording: photo terms require separate written consent for public display and none is recorded, while recording permission and ownership are unconfirmed ([photo terms](<archive/03-rights/photo-terms.txt>), [sound terms](<archive/03-rights/sound-terms.txt>)).

   **Next steps:** Check whether the listed card, scraps, scissors, and tape are still available ([craft box](<archive/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt>)); make a quick paper mock-up; confirm the three-slit pattern with both makers if practical; and ask library staff to confirm a date before preparing the table ([venue](<archive/04-resources/venue.txt>)). The materials check is dated October 2, and the display is not booked.

2. **A low-cost Tide Lines text-and-paper display**

   Make a compact educational display from Mara’s caption drafts and written pier observations, with a simple hand-drawn or paper timeline. The concept is about how water levels reshape familiar paths; the notes include three dated observations and two caption drafts ([concept](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/concept.txt>), [observations](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt>), [text fragments](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt>)). The observations are explicitly a field note, not a scientific dataset, so present them as personal observations rather than scientific evidence. Mara permits reuse of her written notes and captions in free public educational displays ([Tide Lines rights](<archive/03-rights/tide-notes.txt>)).

   **Rights and limits:** Keep the display text-only or use newly made paper elements. The indexed portraits are not included in the archive, identify people, and lack recorded permission for public display; the S-3 recording is also absent and lacks confirmed public-use permission ([photo index](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/photos-index.txt>), [photo description](<archive/02-assets/notes/photo-description.txt>), [photo terms](<archive/03-rights/photo-terms.txt>), [sound index](<archive/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt>), [sound terms](<archive/03-rights/sound-terms.txt>)). The library note about the path moving inland in 1981 needs verification against its original reference before publication ([research](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt>)); omit that historical claim until verified.

   **Next steps:** Draft a one-page layout using the permitted writing, check current paper supplies, and confirm printer availability. The recorded copy-shop quote is $8 for up to twelve black-and-white pages, within the $30 limit, but expires next month ([printing quote](<archive/04-resources/printing-quote.txt>)); the studio printing note also makes availability conditional ([printing note](<archive/02-assets/notes/printing.txt>)). Confirm the library date and any display requirements before printing.

3. **Hypothesis: combine the two projects as a “changing shoreline” table**

   A single free educational table could pair the FW-7 movable bands with Tide Lines captions and observations: the paper model gives visitors something to manipulate, while the notes provide a local example. The combination is grounded in the Folded Water workshop’s changing-shoreline activity and Tide Lines’ changing-water-level theme ([workshop](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt>), [concept](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/concept.txt>)).

   **Why this remains unresolved:** The two rights records separately support the proposed narrow uses, but do not explicitly address combining or adapting the materials together. Keep each contribution identifiable, credit both Folded Water makers and Mara, and confirm that the makers are comfortable with the combined presentation before using it. Do not treat the combination as permission to include third-party photos or sound.

   **Next steps:** Sketch the layout using only the described pattern and Mara’s permitted writing, then seek confirmation from the makers and the library before producing it.

## Resources and scope

Mara has one weekend and a $30 maximum; she is free Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning, but the library table is only a possibility until staff confirm a date ([request](<archive/04-resources/request.txt>), [calendar](<archive/04-resources/calendar.txt>), [venue](<archive/04-resources/venue.txt>)). The old Tide Lines plan depended on a large projector and framed photos, and the earlier Folded Water lightbox was never ordered; a projector and framing supplies are unavailable ([Tide Lines budget](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/budget-draft.txt>), [Folded Water old plan](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/old-plan.txt>), [other materials](<archive/04-resources/other-materials.txt>)). The archive also says old art pens were used up, so they should not be counted as current supplies ([receipts](<archive/05-archive/receipts.txt>)).

I reviewed the files listed in the workspace inventory across project notes, asset notes, rights, resources, and archive records. This is coverage of the listed textual archive, not proof that no other files or permissions exist. The photo files themselves are absent, and the sound index says the recording is not present. No proposal assumes legal clearance beyond the specific written permissions cited above.

All scenarios are fictional text-only descriptions, not real images, videos, audio, stencil files or physical materials. A reasonable candidate is a small educational display combining Tide Lines' written observations/captions (`01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt`, `text-fragments.txt`) with Folded Water's three-band paper technique (`01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt`, `shape-diagram.txt`); available paper/scissors are tentative (`02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt`) and printing is $8 if available (`04-resources/printing-quote.txt`), with a library table subject to confirmation (`04-resources/venue.txt`). The three-slit pattern is later than a two-slit draft, but there is no final signoff: do not assert authoritative status. Any actual physical prototype needs fabrication, venue/date confirmation, and human review. No one owes participants a project; a different well-supported creative proposal can score well.

A: `03-rights/tide-notes.txt` allows Mara's written notes/captions for a free educational display; `03-rights/folded-water.txt` allows FW-7 for that use with maker credits and no commercial resale. `03-rights/photo-terms.txt` requires additional written consent for all public display of P-14–16; audio S-3 is not in the archive and rights unknown. A non-photo, non-audio exhibit drawing on both projects is plausible as a text-only proposal, subject to venue, materials, timing and permissions checks. No legal clearance.
## Recommended concepts

1. **A participatory “changing shoreline” paper display.** Rework the *Folded Water* workshop as a small table activity: visitors move three blue paper bands against a white card silhouette to see how one shape can suggest a changing shoreline. The workshop already explored that idea, and its notes say movement made changes easy to notice ([demo notes](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt>), [workshop](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt>)). The described FW-7 pattern makes a portable three-band silhouette ([shape diagram](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt>)); the archive lists card, blue scraps, scissors, and tape, though availability should be checked ([materials](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt>), [craft box](<archive/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt>)).

   **Next steps:** Confirm current supplies and a table date with library staff; make a paper prototype and check whether the three-slit description is workable. The January draft says two slits while the later workshop record says three, and there is no final signoff ([old copy](<archive/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt>)). The rights note permits FW-7 in a free community educational display with credit to both makers, but excludes commercial resale ([Folded Water rights](<archive/03-rights/folded-water.txt>)).

2. **A compact “Tide Lines” reading table.** Pair Mara’s short captions with a clearly labeled, non-scientific sequence of three pier observations. The archive has reusable captions ([text fragments](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt>)) and observations from three dates, explicitly described as field notes rather than a scientific dataset ([observations](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt>)). Mara permits reuse of these notes and captions in free public educational displays ([Tide Lines rights](<archive/03-rights/tide-notes.txt>)).

   **Next steps:** Draft a few black-and-white pages within the shared studio’s limit of 12 pages for $8, checking printer availability first ([printing](<archive/02-assets/notes/printing.txt>)). Confirm the library date and keep the presentation descriptive rather than making scientific claims. The historical claim about the inlet path moving inland in 1981 needs verification from its original reference before publication ([research](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt>)).

3. **A combined paper-and-text activity table.** A single free educational table could pair the movable shoreline bands with the Tide Lines captions, giving visitors both a hands-on activity and a short reading prompt. This combines the documented workshop concept and available text permissions ([Folded Water workshop](<archive/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt>), [Tide Lines text](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt>), [Tide Lines rights](<archive/03-rights/tide-notes.txt>)).

   **Next steps:** Prototype the paper element, select a small set of captions, and confirm supplies, printing, and the library booking. Keep the two projects’ credits and permissions clear: FW-7 requires credit to both makers, and Tide Lines permission covers Mara’s writing only ([Folded Water rights](<archive/03-rights/folded-water.txt>), [Tide Lines rights](<archive/03-rights/tide-notes.txt>)).

## Constraints and uncertainties

All three concepts fit the stated one-weekend, $30 maximum, and free educational-display scope in principle ([request](<archive/04-resources/request.txt>)). The venue is only possible pending staff confirmation, not booked ([venue](<archive/04-resources/venue.txt>)); Mara’s listed weekend availability is Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning ([calendar](<archive/04-resources/calendar.txt>)). The printer quote is $8 for up to 12 black-and-white pages and expires next month ([printing quote](<archive/04-resources/printing-quote.txt>)).

Avoid using the indexed portraits or sound recording unless their separate permissions are confirmed: the photo terms require written photographer consent, and the sound’s ownership and public-use permission are unconfirmed ([photo terms](<archive/03-rights/photo-terms.txt>), [sound terms](<archive/03-rights/sound-terms.txt>)). The image files and recording are absent from this archive ([photo index](<archive/01-projects/tide-lines/photos-index.txt>), [sound index](<archive/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt>)). No proposal here assumes that any missing permission has been obtained.The archive supports **two modest proposals** for a free community educational display. The venue is only possible, not booked, and its dates need confirmation with staff ([venue.txt](archive/04-resources/venue.txt)). Mara has one weekend and a $30 maximum ([request.txt](archive/04-resources/request.txt)).

1. **A movable “changing shoreline” paper demonstration.** Use white card, blue paper, scissors, and masking tape to show how moving bands can represent a changing shoreline. The prototype used card, blue offcuts, and scissors; the workshop notes say the movable bands made changes easy to notice ([materials.txt](archive/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt), [demo-notes.txt](archive/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt)). Pattern FW-7 is described as one folded card with three horizontal slits, but there is no finished stencil ([shape-diagram.txt](archive/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt)). Mara and her collaborator permit its use in a free community display, with credit to both makers; commercial resale is excluded ([folded-water.txt](archive/03-rights/folded-water.txt)).  
   **Next steps:** Check that the shelf materials are still available ([craft-box.txt](archive/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt)); make and test a paper model; credit both makers; and confirm the display date. The older two-slit draft conflicts with the later three-slit workshop record, and the archive has no final-authoritative signoff ([old-copy.txt](archive/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt)). The abandoned motorized lightbox is not a practical option because it was never ordered and is unavailable ([old-plan.txt](archive/01-projects/folded-water/old-plan.txt)).

2. **A small Tide Lines text-and-observation display.** Pair Mara’s short captions with the three dated water-level observations and invite visitors to consider how a crossing changes with the tide ([text-fragments.txt](archive/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt), [observations.txt](archive/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt)). Mara permits reuse of her written notes and captions in free public educational displays ([tide-notes.txt](archive/03-rights/tide-notes.txt)). The observations are field notes, not a scientific dataset, so describe them that way.  
   **Next steps:** Draft a concise, text-only handout or table display. If printing is available, up to twelve black-and-white pages cost $8, though printer availability should be checked on the day ([printing.txt](archive/02-assets/notes/printing.txt)); the separate copy-shop quote is $8 for up to twelve pages and expires next month ([printing-quote.txt](archive/04-resources/printing-quote.txt)). Confirm the date and budget before printing.

I would leave the photo and sound assets out of either proposal. The photo agreement requires separate written consent for public display, and none is recorded; the recording’s public-use permission is unconfirmed ([photo-terms.txt](archive/03-rights/photo-terms.txt), [sound-terms.txt](archive/03-rights/sound-terms.txt)). The historical claim about the inlet path moving inland in 1981 also needs checking against its original reference before publication ([research.txt](archive/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt)).

The archive does not establish that supplies remain available, that the printer will work, or that the library table is booked. Both concepts look feasible within the stated time and budget if those practical details check out; no rights clearance beyond the specific written permissions above is established.
